notes.summary:
Customer support agents spend their working day navigating a high-pressure environment defined by ticket management, real-time communication, and internal collaboration. Their time is largely consumed by the "triage" of incoming inquiries, manual documentation of case details, and the effort to meet strict response time expectations.

### Daily Computer Tasks & Workflow
Agents spend the majority of their time inside a primary "Help Desk" platform (e.g., Zendesk, Front, Intercom) which acts as their central hub.
*   **Ticket Management:** Agents spend significant time monitoring queues, categorizing incoming requests, and searching knowledge bases for accurate solutions.
*   **Communication Load:** Agents juggle multiple channels—email, live chat, SMS, and occasionally voice. Email remains the slowest, most time-consuming channel, often requiring agents to synthesize information from long conversation threads.
*   **Documentation & Admin:** A large portion of the day is spent updating CRM records, summarizing past interactions, and manually logging details that are not automatically captured.
*   **Automation Interaction:** Modern agents increasingly spend time reviewing and editing AI-suggested responses rather than typing answers from scratch.

### Apps Used on Mac
Support teams on macOS typically use a mix of web-based platforms and dedicated desktop clients.
*   **Help Desk/Omnichannel Tools:** **Zendesk**, **Front**, **Missive**, **Help Scout**, and **Freshdesk** are industry standards.
    *   *Note:* Many of these are Electron-based apps (web wrappers). **Moorline** is a notable native Swift app for Mac users seeking deeper OS integration.
*   **Communication & Collaboration:** **Slack** is frequently used for internal coordination with engineers or managers when a ticket requires escalation.
*   **Productivity:** **Apple Mail** is sometimes used for lower-volume support, though it lacks the ticket-tracking capabilities of dedicated help desk software.

### Key Statistics
| Metric | Finding | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Email Response Gap** | The average business email response time is **12 hours and 10 minutes**, despite 88–89% of customers expecting a reply within 60 minutes. | SuperOffice / Various |
| **Email Load** | Employees spend up to **28% of their workweek** managing email, receiving an average of 121 messages daily. | Speakwise |
| **Non-Response Rate** | **62% of businesses** fail to respond to customer service emails entirely. | SuperOffice |
| **AI Efficiency** | AI-powered support tools have been shown to compress resolution times from **32 hours down to 32 minutes** in some contexts. | StealthAgents |

### Caveats
*   **Tooling Discrepancies:** While many tools are "web-only," some (like Front or Missive) offer desktop applications that provide a more "native" feel on macOS, though they may consume more memory due to their Electron architecture.
*   **Metric Definitions:** "Average response time" statistics vary significantly depending on whether the source measures *first response time* (the initial acknowledgment) or *resolution time* (total time to fix the issue). Always verify if a study includes automated acknowledgments in its response time data.
